newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Dominion Mining eyes Canada listing.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Dominion Mining eyes Canada listing.

text.p: Dominion Mining NL said on Wednesday it was considering a Canadian listing as a part of its overall plan to expedite the development of its Yakabindie nickel project in Western Australia.
Asked if the company was looking at a Canadian listing, Dominion chairman, Peter Joseph said: "That's one of the options. There is quite a bit of interest in nickel in that country."
The Yakabindie project has proven and probable reserves of 193 million tonnes grading 0.51 percent nickel and a resource of 293 million tonnes grading 0.525 percent nickel.

Speaking earlier at the company's annual meeting, Joseph said a revised mining reserves and formulation of a new mine plan had made the A$500 milion project more attractive since 15 percent shareholder North Ltd decided in December last year not to take up an option for an 80 percent stake.

"There is more interest (in the project) than less interets and I think that has a lot to do with the fact that the project economics and the project definition have improved a lot over the last four months," Joseph said.

Under a revised development strategy announced by Dominion earlier this year, the Yakabindie project is planned to be in production during the third quarter of 1997 with mining of a small relatively high grade deposit and fast track construction of a 500,000 tonnes ore per annum plant.

Dominion said stage one had an estimated capital development cost of A$35 million and would provide a further opportunity to prove the processing technology at a commercial scale and assure financiers of the project's viability.
Joseph said it was becoming increasingly evident that Yakabindie would be strong enough to be launched on a project basis without further recourse to shareholders.
Dominion shares closed five cents firmer at 81 cents.
